title: Shabbat Chicken with Leeks & Mushrooms, Olive-Oil Mashed Potatoes & Sweet Peas
summary: Dairy-free Shabbat chicken thighs braised with tender leeks and mushrooms, served with olive-oil mashed potatoes and sweet peas. Approximately 50 minutes total, 30–35 minutes active. Make ahead and hold hot safely before Shabbat.
ingredients: 2 lb kosher boneless skinless chicken thighs
2 medium leeks, white and light-green parts only, thoroughly washed and sliced
3 tbsp olive oil, divided, plus more as needed
¾ cup kosher-certified dairy-free chicken broth, plus ¼–½ cup for potatoes
2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled or scrubbed and cut into chunks
instructions: Put potato chunks in a pot of salted water, bring to a boil and simmer 15–20 minutes until fork-tender.
Season chicken with paprika, thyme, salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a deep skillet and sear chicken 3–4 minutes per side; remove to a plate.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil, leeks and mushrooms to the skillet; sauté 6–8 minutes until soft. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add ¾ cup dairy-free chicken broth, return chicken and juices, cover and simmer gently 15–20 minutes until the thickest chicken pieces reach at least 165°F.
Drain potatoes and mash with remaining olive oil and ¼–½ cup warm dairy-free broth until fluffy. Season to taste. Never add butter, milk or cream.
Warm peas in a small covered pot with a splash of water for 3–4 minutes; drain. Serve with chicken, leek-mushroom sauce and mashed potatoes.
child_friendly_modifications: Reserve a couple of lightly seasoned chicken pieces and serve chopped, with plain mashed potatoes and peas in separate piles. Offer the leek-mushroom sauce on the side. Mash peas lightly for younger children if needed.
leftovers: Refrigerate within two hours and use within 3–4 days. Shred leftover chicken into dairy-free potato bowls with warmed peas and leek sauce; reheat to 165°F.
shabbat_preparation: Prepare completely before Shabbat, or make a day ahead and refrigerate promptly. Before Shabbat, reheat thoroughly to 165°F and use a Shabbat-compliant warming arrangement that maintains food at 140°F or hotter; follow family halachic practice. Keep chicken covered with sauce and potatoes covered with a little broth so neither dries out.
